newsitem.title: USA: Shell says US Gulf oil/gas platform back.
newsitem.headline: Shell says US Gulf oil/gas platform back.

text.p: Shell Oil Co said Friday that its Auger oil and gas platform in the U.S. Gulf of Mexico, shut last weekend for expansion work, came back on line early this morning.

"Auger came back on line at one a.m. (0100 CST). The expectation is that it will come back at about the same production level as before," a company spokeswoman said, adding she was not sure what exact flows were now but the platform had been producing 75,000 barrels per day (bpd) of crude and 160,000 million cubic feet per day (mmcfd) of natural gas prior to shutdown.
The company had expected the platform, which is located in Garden Banks block 426, to resume production Thursday morning.
The spokeswoman said the expansion work should result in increased flows of about 100,000 bpd of crude and 300 mmcfd of gas by mid-year.
Shell Oil Co is the U.S.-based unit of Anglo-Dutch Royal Dutch/Shell.
